newsitem.title: COSTA RICA: U.S. Peace Corps volunteer missing in Costa Rica.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Peace Corps volunteer missing in Costa Rica.

text.p: A U.S. Peace Corps volunteer disappeared while hiking in the mountains of Costa Rica a week ago, Red Cross officials said on Thursday.
A four-day air-and-ground search for Elizabeth Livingston, 48, failed to turn up clues, officials said.

Livingston, an avid hiker from Santa Fe, New Mexico, told friends she intended to visit the site where a small plane crashed in 1990 in a remote area about 10 miles (15 km) southwest of San Jose, Red Cross spokesman Luis Baharona told Reuters.
Livingston lived in the tiny mountainside village of El Carmen just outside San Jose and would often hike through the farms and forests of the surrounding hills, friends said.
A group of hikers reported seeing Livingston last Thursday hiking alone, around a 45-minute walk from the crash site, Guillermo Aroyo, Red Cross chief of rescue operations, told reporters.
The search began on Monday after friends reported her missing on Sunday, Baharona said.
He said 70 people between Red Cross officials, Civil Guard and police canine units were involved in the search, as well as a small and a helicopter.
